NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have received a complaint from Akashvani staffers against Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, as well as the MPs and others accompanying them, for allegedly forcing their way into the Akashvani office.Rahul and Priyanka were briefly detained on Tuesday night after an over eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan premises. The protest began after police stopped INDIA bloc MPs from marching towards the Election Commission's office, around 300 metres away, over allegations of "vote chori".Rahul had entered the All India Radio premises on Parliament Street around noon and joined the protest.Earlier, during the march from Parliament towards the EC headquarters, he climbed atop barricades as opposition MPs raised slogans of "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod". Police said around 250 people, including 50 MPs, were detained on Tuesday night following the prolonged sit-in. Gandhi and other Congress leaders were released around 10 pm, the party said.The opposition MPs were protesting over "vote chori" allegations and seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar in the wake of media reports alleging differences within the Election Commission over the SIR of electoral rolls and other issues.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Pawan Khera on Tuesday warned the government that the INDIA bloc’s protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was only the beginning, shortly after opposition MPs were released from New Police Lines in Kingsway Camp.“The words being spoken today are going to cost them dearly. The people of this country know exactly how to deal with such words and the people who utter them,” Khera told reporters after his release. He said those in power should “mend their ways right now” and warned that the public would “bring down those who are currently riding the high horse of arrogance”.Khera named Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Union home minister Amit Shah, saying they “will not sleep tonight—nor will they sleep soundly ever again—because they have betrayed the nation”.“If Gyanesh Kumar thinks that just because we went home today, it is all over, he needs to understand that this is merely the beginning—nothing has ended yet,” Khera said.Earlier on Tuesday, Delhi Police detained Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi along with several other Congress MPs from near Akashvani Bhavan following a day-long protest demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The INDIA bloc MPs had marched from the Parliament complex towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters, seeking a meeting with the election commissioners over their allegations of “vote chori”.Police stopped the march near Akashvani Bhavan, following which the MPs staged a sit-in.After nearly nine hours of protest, police moved in and detained several opposition MPs, including Khera, KC Venugopal and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring. Around 50 MPs were detained and taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp, according to PTI, citing sources.“The Election Commission office is barely 50 metres away, but we were not allowed to go there. I don't know what's happening in the country,” Rahul said.“If the representatives of the people cannot meet the Election Commission, then what is the meaning of democracy?” he said.

Article Title: Ashok Chakra for flydubai pilot Smit Machchar? Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma urges PM Modi
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha member seeks Ashok Chakra for Indian pilot Smit Machchar

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kartikeya Sharma has written to PM Modi , urging him to consider awarding the country's highest peacetime gallantry award, the 'Ashok Chakra' to flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchar for his courage and presence of mind midair during a hijacking attempt made by Omani co-pilot.Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30 after his co-pilot attacked him and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Despite suffering severe injuries, Machchar remained focused on protecting the 174 passengers on board and continued to carry out his duties under extreme circumstances.Sharma said Machchar's courage and composure during the crisis reflected the "indomitable spirit" and dedication to duty of Indians. He said the captain put the safety of passengers ahead of his own well-being despite being seriously injured.The Rajya Sabha member said recognising Machchar at the national level would not only honour his bravery but also inspire young people across the country. He added that every Indian was proud of the captain's courage.Sharma urged Prime Minister Modi to consider conferring the 'Ashok Chakra' on Machchar in recognition of his bravery and dedication to duty.The letter comes days after the alleged hijacking attempt aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. According to reports, Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe inside the cockpit in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot.The confrontation caused the aircraft to enter a steep descent, with the plane dropping around 16,000 feet in two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was sent.The aircraft was later diverted and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board disembarked safely.A Times of Israel report published on Sunday said al-Hammami had planned to direct the aircraft towards Israel's Ben Gurion Airport.The report, citing Hebrew media sources, said the Omani co-pilot was detained and was being interrogated in the United Arab Emirates.
Article Summary: Rajya sabha member seeks ashok chakra for indian pilot smit machchar. Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight fz1073 on september 30. Omani co-pilot hamam al-hammami attacked machchar with an axe inside the cockpit.

Article Title: How will economy be impacted if India-US trade deal doesn’t happen? RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra answers
Article Text:
Malhotra’s comments come within days of FM Sitharaman indicating discussions having "reached a plateau”.

Where India-US trade deal talks stand

India’s trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible US tariffs if a trade deal does not come through, indicated RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday.Asked about the possible impact on the economy if the India-US trade deal is not finalised, Malhotra said, “The impact depends on what extent tariffs are going to be applied. So it's premature to answer. But obviously, it will have some negative impact.”“At the same time, we have had a number of trade agreements now in the recent past. Some of them have been operationalized, others are in the pipeline. They will help. The industry at the same time has diversified its exports,” Malhotra said at the post monetary policy press conference.“So all these things will mitigate the effect in case there is an additional tariff on some of the sectors,” he added.Also Read | Will Russian oil be economically viable for India if Trump tariffs return? Malhotra’s comments come within days of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicating that the India-US bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked, with discussions having "reached a plateau”.Sitharaman’s remarks came a few days after US Trade Representative (USTR) Jaimeson Greer indicated that an agreement was not close."I don't think there's something imminent, but we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points. We're working diligently toward them," he said after his meeting with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Trump also discussed bilateral trade during a phone conversation last week, along with defence, energy and other matters.Meanwhile, Sitharaman said, “The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it," she said at the Munich Security Conference.Also Read | ‘Rate cuts off the table’: Why RBI hiked repo rate by 25 basis points but also raised GDP growth forecast to 7.1% Sitharaman said the US would look to narrow its trade deficit with India, which stood at an estimated $34 billion last year, down from $41 billion in 2024-25. The gap could reduce further as India has increased its purchases of energy from the US.Officials from India and the US have continued negotiations on the trade agreement and have repeatedly indicated that the talks were close to being concluded. The US has been pushing for greater access for its agricultural products in India through lower tariffs. However, the recent law permitting duties of up to 100% on imports of Russian oil is viewed as another hurdle in the negotiations.An agreement, in any case, can be finalised only after the Indian government has clarity on the extent of additional tariffs that could be imposed on its exports. At present, the USTR has imposed an additional duty of 10-12.5% on more than 50 countries, citing their alleged failure to prevent imports of goods produced using forced labour. The US is also examining structural overcapacity in countries including India, a charge that India has denied.In February, India and the US had agreed on a bilateral trade agreement under which the Trump administration imposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the arrangement was put on hold after the Supreme Court ruled that the “reciprocal tariffs” were illegal.
Article Summary: Rbi governor sanjay malhotra said india's trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible us tariffs if a trade deal does not come through. His comments come within days of finance minister nirmala sitharaman indicating that the india-us bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked.

Article Title: 'Making steady progress, regaining health': Indian embassy in UAE updates on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar
Article Text:
Capt. Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani national with a crash axe.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar is “making steady progress” and “regaining his health” after being seriously injured in an attack by his co-pilot on a flydubai flight last week, the Indian Embassy in the UAE said on Tuesday.Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an Omani national with a crash axe, an emergency tool typically kept in the cockpit during flydubai flight FZ1073 on Wednesday. The motive for the attack remains unclear.“Capt Smit continues to make steady progress and is regaining his health. The Embassy remains in close touch with his family, doctors & local authorities, extending all possible assistance,” the embassy said in a post on X.“We thank everyone for their prayers & wish him a speedy recovery,” it added.The flight, carrying 174 passengers, sent emergency signals after the attack and rapidly descended more than 17,000 feet from an altitude of 34,000 feet.Machchhar, who was lying injured on the cockpit floor, realised that the aircraft was descending and made “one last push” to open the cockpit door.He managed to activate the door release despite being seriously injured and covered in blood.Two reserve pilots then took control of the aircraft and landed it safely at Prince Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The co-pilot was taken into custody, while Machchhar was taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.Machchhar was initially admitted to a hospital in Tabuk before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi for further medical treatment, PTI reported.On October 1, India's ambassador to the UAE, Deepak Mittal, had said Machchhar was “in good health and recovering well”. Mittal had also visited the injured captain and his family at the hospital.The investigation into the attack is ongoing, with the motive behind the co-pilot's actions still unclear.
Article Summary: Capt. Smit machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot, an omani national with a crash axe. The motive for the attack remains unclear. The flight, carrying 174 passengers, sent emergency signals after the attack and rapidly descended more than 17,000 feet.

Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Article Text:
What Bhuyan had said

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.
Article Summary: Former chief justice of india br gavai and other retired judges on monday condemned supreme court judge justice ujjal bhuyan's remarks on the election commission. Justice dhingra said bhuian's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" justice sodhi said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework.

Article Title: 'Inflation man Modi's reign of terror continues': Congress on repo rate hike
Article Text:
Congress slams Centre after RBI raises repo rate to 5.5%

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, saying the move would further increase the financial burden on the public.Calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi “inflation man”, the Congress said, “Inflation Man Modi's reign of terror continues. Now the public's back will be broken even further.”The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans, resulting in higher EMIs and potentially longer repayment periods. “To curb inflation as per Modi's intent, the RBI has today raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%,” it said."This means your home loan, car loan, personal loan, and business loan interest rates will now increase. Now you'll have to pay higher EMIs, and the loan repayment period will also get extended. The promise was of 'good days,' but what we got were days of extortion," he added.The RBI's monetary policy committee unanimously approved the hike and shifted its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, citing stronger-than-expected economic growth and broader price pressures.The rate increase would raise the monthly EMI on a Rs 1 crore home loan with a 15-year tenure by around Rs 1,500, assuming a base rate of 8.50%. If borrowers keep their EMI unchanged, the higher interest rate could extend the repayment period by roughly six instalments.The RBI also raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, while increasing its inflation projection by 20 basis points to 5.2%. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said stronger capacity utilisation, bank credit growth, government capital expenditure and infrastructure spending were supporting investment and demand.CPI inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July. Malhotra said price pressures had broadened beyond volatile items, with food inflation becoming more widespread, including higher sugar and onion prices.The Congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”.
Article Summary: Congress slams centre after rbi raises repo rate to 5.5% to curb inflation. Party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans, resulting in higher emis. The congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”

Article Title: 'Unable to distinguish between victim & perpetrator': India tears into OIC over J&K remarks at UN
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India hit back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly, rejecting its remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and New Delhi’s actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.West Tripura Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb, delivering India’s national statement at the UNGA Sixth Committee on Tuesday said the OIC had failed to distinguish between those responsible for terrorism and its victims.“I also address now the statement delivered by the chair of the OIC on India's focused and measured actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, from where terrorist attacks against India were planned and directed,” news agency PTI quoted Deb saying.He added that it is “regrettable that those delivering the statement” are “unable to separate fact from fiction and distinguish between victim and perpetrator”.India asserted that it has the right to defend its citizens against cross-border terrorism and warned that there would be consequences for those who engage in terrorism.Deb also objected to what he called the OIC’s “unwarranted reference” to Jammu and Kashmir.He urged the grouping to instead focus on Pakistan’s “illegal occupation” and alleged rights violations in PoK.“The OIC chair would do better to focus on Pakistan's illegal occupation, especially in Rawalakot, where wanton killings, brutal violence and the denial of basic rights to the people living there are so visible. Such willful blindness only speaks of bigotry and intolerance,” he said.Saudi Arabia had delivered the OIC statement at the Sixth Committee, which deals with legal issues. The OIC referred to “military escalation in Southeast Asia” and “unjustified strikes” at multiple locations in Pakistan, without naming India.India’s response came as it reiterated its position that cross-border terrorism remains a persistent threat. Deb cited the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 civilians were killed, and said the attack demonstrated the human cost of terrorism.“The Pahalgam terror attack was a calculated assault on our sovereignty, planned and executed by networks that continue to enjoy state patronage, safe havens, and material and logistical support from across our western border,” he said.Deb also called terrorism one of the gravest threats to international peace and security, stressing that there could be no justification for attacks on civilians.“Terrorism is antithetical to the values of the UN. There can be no justification whatsoever for deliberately targeting civilians. There is no distinction between good and bad terrorism,” he said.

Article Title: Three new SC judges take oath, all in the name of God; number of women judges in SC – three out of 37

NEW DELHI: Three new Supreme Court Judges – Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh – on Tuesday took oath of office in the name of God taking the working strength of SC to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.CJI Surya Kant administered oath to Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya and Singh, who were chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana HCs respectively, in the presence of SC judges, attorney general R Venkataramani, solicitor general Tushar Mehta and other senior advocates and lawyers.With the elevation of Justice Agarwal, who is the 13th women judge of SC, the strength of women judges in the apex court at present became three. The other two being Justices B V Nagarathna, who is scheduled to become the first woman CJI on Sep 24 next year, and Justice V Mohana.During the tenure of Justice N V Ramana as CJI, the Supreme Court had the highest number of sitting SC judges at four – Justices India Banerjee, Nagarathna, Hima Kohli and Bela M Trivedi, last three of whom had taken oath on Aug 31, 2021. While the Collegium led by Justice Ramana had recommended appointment of three women judges, the present collegium led by CJI Kant has so far appointed two women judges.SC got its first woman judge in M Fathima Beevi on Oct 6, 1989, 39 years after SC was established. Justice Beevi had retired from Kerala HC on Apr 29, 1989, but was elevated to the SC five months after retirement. Other women judges in SC were – Justices Sujata V Manohar, Ruma Pal, Gyan Sudha Misra, Ranjana P Desai, R Bhanumathi and Indu Malhotra.SC judge strength was increased from 34 to 38, including the CJI, initially through an Ordinance on May 16. The corresponding Amendment Act was passed by Parliament which received the President's assent on Aug 11. In Aug 2019, during the tenure of CJI Ranjan Gogoi, the sanctioned strength of SC judges was increased from 31 to 34, including CJI.The SC had started in 1950 with a sanctioned strength of 8 Judges, which was increased to 11 in 1956, 14 in 1960, 18 in 1978, 26 in 1986, and 31 in 2009. SC as of Tuesday has a pendency of 95, 481 cases.
Article Summary: Three new supreme court judges – justices sunita agarwal, devendra kumar upadhyaya and aparesh kumar singh – on tuesday took oath of office in the name of god. Their appointment takes the working strength of sc to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.

Article Title: Modi's 25 years in office: A study in seva and action
Article Text:
File photo

(The writer is the president, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, Global Guide of Heartfulness Meditation)

In a democracy, when someone completes 25 consecutive years as the head of a govt, it is indeed special. I heartily congratulate Shri Narendra Modi ji on 25 glorious years of service as head of govt. He is someone I am very fond of and someone I have interacted with closely over the years.Who is Modiji? What makes him successful? What drives him? These are very common questions and are worth pondering over.For me, Prime Minister Modi is a blend of both leadership and spirituality.When I reflect upon the life of Narendrabhai, one quality that draws my attention is this sense of an underlying purpose running through very different phases of his life. I have often spoken of the divided heart - a heart pulled in many directions by competing desires. There is an inherent tension between freedom and desire, between what is pleasant and what is good. Aspirants on the spiritual path encounter this tension and have to work at resolving it before real progress is possible.In Narendrabhai's life, we can see that this work happened quite early on. I recently learned that at seventeen, he left home, travelled across India and spent time in the Himalayas; influenced by Swami Vivekananda and his encounters with different communities and traditions, his life began to orient itself towards service.Thereafter, the outer form kept changing - from pracharak to organiser, from CM to PM, but the idea of service remained a recurring thread. When the heart becomes united in purpose, positions cease to be destinations in themselves. They become different instruments through which that purpose can find expression.The devastating flood at Morbi in 1979, following failure of the Machchhu dam, gave this commitment a demanding field of action. Narendrabhai worked there as a volunteer in the aftermath of disaster. Years later, while visiting landslide-affected Wayanad in 2024, he recalled that experience as helping him understand suffering of families who'd lost so much. When we serve people in their hour of distress, their difficulties cease to be concerns. They become responsibilities we feel within ourselves.A sense of purpose finds expression in the way we respond to the person before us. When Seva takes root in the heart, even an ordinary encounter becomes an opportunity to care. An incident from Narendrabhai's earlier life brings this quality to mind.In her account "A train journey and two names to remember," published in The Hindu in 2014, Leena Sarma recalled her journey from Delhi to Ahmedabad in 1990 with Utpalparna Hazarika. Both women were Railway Traffic Service probationers, travelling for the next phase of training without confirmed berths. The ticket examiner found them space in a first-class compartment occupied by Narendra Modi and Shankersinh Vaghela. That evening, Narendrabhai paid for all four vegetarian meals. Later, when the ticket examiner explained that no berths could be arranged for the women, both men surrendered theirs, spread a cloth on the floor and slept there, leaving the berths to the two probationers.What touches me is the ease with which they gave up their comfort. In Sarma's recollection, the kindness came without ceremony. This was long before Narendrabhai became chief minister or Prime Minister, and the need before him was simple and immediate. Such moments invite us to reflect on how we behave when no one is watching as an example of leadership. Can we notice another person's difficulty and respond without seeking recognition? To me, this is generosity of heart. It gives a human warmth to purpose and allows seva to become part of everyday life.Doubt will visit every sincere seeker, just as uncertainty accompanies every person who accepts a great responsibility. If one listens to its whisperings, faith is progressively fractured; the will loses its ability to drive action and real spiritual progress becomes difficult. The question is not whether doubt arises, but whether we allow it to become the driver of our lives. This is where shraddha becomes so important.Shraddha is more than belief; it contains trust, self-confidence, sincerity, determination and inner conviction. I am reminded here of Narendrabhai becoming CM of Gujarat in 2001. At fifty-one, he had never contested an election and had never held an administrative position. He was asked to govern a state still recovering from a devastating earthquake and there were understandable questions about whether an experienced organiser could become an effective administrator. Yet he accepted the responsibility and learnt while carrying it. His early tenure as chief minister was fraught with many challenges that he had to overcome, challenges that could have tested the faith of many.Conviction does not mean that we know beforehand that we will succeed. It means that uncertainty does not prevent us from taking the next step. We may hear the voice of doubt, we may learn from it, but we need not hand over to it the direction of our lives. Narendrabhai's life is one where doubt has never been allowed into the driver's seat; in fact, courage and conviction have been given that place.Fear asks, "What if?" while faith responds, "Even if." Fearlessness does not mean that a human being never experiences fear. What matters is whether fear is permitted to determine our direction. Narendrabhai's life offers examples of accepting responsibility in very different circumstances of uncertainty. In his mid-sixties, when Narendrabhai accepted the mantle of being Prime Minister of India, the scale of uncertainty was enormous: he moved from leading one state to assuming responsibility for India's national security, diplomacy and relationships with the world, at a time when questions were being asked about how a state leader would make that transition.Later came a spell of challenges that may constitute one of the most turbulent periods in recent history. The Covid pandemic, trade wars, the geopolitical upheaval following the war in Ukraine and the recent West Asia crisis, along with domestic challenges, feature among circumstances that would have tested the fortitude of any leader, let alone one who holds the hopes of 1.4 billion. To navigate this with poise is exemplary. Perhaps this is one way of understanding courage spiritually. It is not to say, "Nothing can happen to me." It is to say, "Whatever may happen, I will not allow fear alone to decide what I must do."And so, for any student of leadership, there is a clear lesson from his life. Cultivating a heart free from division, allowing generosity to guide our actions, anchoring mind in conviction and developing a spirit that does not act from fear are spiritual principles that have helped shape Narendrabhai's path as a karmayogi. These principles are universal and when we see them manifest in someone's life, we can use them as inspiration.I take this occasion to wish Narendrabhai all the very best; may the divine grant him a long life to carry forward this era with leadership and guidance, and may he continue to take India to greater and greater heights.
Article Summary: Shri ram chandra mission president congratulates pm on 25 years as head of govt. He says narendrabhai is a blend of leadership and spirituality. When the heart becomes united in purpose, positions cease to be destinations in themselves, he says. Shraddha is more than belief; it contains trust, self-confidence, sincerity, determination and inner conviction.

Article Title: US House introduces resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar, condemns 'act of terrorism'
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi hospital from multiple injuries

Resolved, That the House of Representatives— (1) honors Captain Smit Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft; (2) commends the heroic actions of the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down; (3) wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery; (4) condemns the attack on Flydubai Flight 1073 as an act of terrorism and as an attack on the safety of international civil aviation; and (5) calls for a full and expeditious investigation by the Governments of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.

The US House of Representatives have introduced a resolution honouring Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar who was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami on September 30.The resolution introduced as "Honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on that flight" by Josh Gottheimer, Don Bacon and Michael McCaul, described the incident and hailed Machchhar."On September 30, 2026, Flydubai Flight 1073 departed Dubai International Airport for Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, Israel, carrying approximately 174 passengers, the majority of them Israeli citizens, including 4 United States citizens and 27 children," it stated."Whereas, midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain on the flight deck with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and attempted to seize the flight controls, and the aircraft lost more than 14,000 feet of altitude in under 30 seconds," it desribed the incident. Whereas Captain Smit Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and, despite grave injuries, used his remaining strength to unlock the cockpit door so that off-duty pilots could enter and land the aircraft and so that crew and passengers could restrain the first officer; Whereas the aircraft landed safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia with all passengers and crew accounted for; and Whereas, on October 3, 2026, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the Emirati investigation had determined that the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act," it added.Then it went to resolve as follows:On September 30, Flydubai Flight FZ1073, carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was forced into an emergency diversion after the co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft.The plane rapidly lost altitude before Machchhar, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker; two off-duty pilots then helped land the aircraft safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The UAE subsequently launched an investigation, and on October 3 its Attorney General said the probe had found that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act. Investigators are continuing to examine the circumstances, motive, possible links and physical and digital evidence, with authorities in other countries also looking into the incident.
Article Summary: Smit machchhar is recovering in abu dhabi hospital from multiple injuries. He was stabbed by his omani co-pilot hamam al-hammami on september 30. Two off-duty pilots then helped land the aircraft safely in tabuk, saudi arabia.

Article Title: The India mood: The country is going places. Will my career follow?
Article Text:

A sense of collective pride, and yet a feeling of individual disquiet. This is probably the most accurate description of the mood among India's more connected, urban-skewed population. There is confidence in the larger macroeconomic story, even as there is lingering uncertainty about the jobs market and an apparent weakening of the old assumption that education is a sure-shot route to upward mobility. Ipsos's September surveys capture that dilemma between hope and anxiety. India ranks first among 30 markets on consumer confidence but 16th on jobs, and unemployment is the issue Indian respondents worry about most.India's consumers are upbeat about the economy. In Ipsos's September 2026 Global Consumer Confidence Index, India scores 66.9, the highest among the 30 markets, compared with a global average of 48.4. Ipsos says its India sample is more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population and hence the results should be read as reflecting the views of a more "connected" segment.India's Current Index, an indicator of how people rate present conditions, is 70.7, and its Investment Index is 73.2, both the highest among the 30 markets in the published survey.Its Expectations Index, at 66.4, ranks fourth, so respondents are also buoyant about the future.The contrast is particularly sharp against the world's major advanced economies. Among the G7, the US has the highest overall consumer-confidence score at 50.5, followed by Great Britain at 48.2 and Canada at 47.3. Italy scores 43.0, Germany 41.4, France 40.6 and Japan 39.4. India, at 66.9, is therefore 16.4 points above the best-performing G7 economy.Across the countries surveyed, India is the most confident market, followed by Sweden at 60.0 and Malaysia at 54.8. At the other end, Türkiye is lowest at 35.3, followed by Argentina at 37.8 and Japan at 39.4. The gap between India and Türkiye is more than 31 points. Only one number breaks the pattern. India's Jobs Index is 59.3, putting it in 16th spot. On current conditions and investment, India sits more than 30 points above the 30-country average. On jobs, its lead is just 1.6 points.In the September edition of Ipsos's What Worries the World survey, 47% of Indian respondents name unemployment among the three issues they find most worrying in the country, making it the most frequently cited concern in India. The global average is 29%. South Africa, Argentina, Singapore, Indonesia and Chile are the only countries with a higher share of respondents citing unemployment as a worry.Among the G7, unemployment is cited as a top concern by 28% in Canada and Italy, 20% in the US, 19% in Great Britain, 16% in France and 13% each in Germany and Japan, well below India's 47%. Across the 30 countries surveyed, concern is highest in South Africa, at 69%, and lowest in the Netherlands, at 6%.The same survey also finds strong optimism among Indian respondents. Seventy per cent say the country is heading in the right direction, against a global average of 38%. Only Singapore, at 80%, records a higher figure. Meanwhile, 79% describe the current economic situation in India as good, again compared with a global average of 38%.Here too India stands apart from the G7. The share saying their country is heading in the right direction is 44% in Canada, 36% in Japan, 28% in Great Britain, 27% in the US, 23% in Italy, 14% in Germany and 11% in France. Singapore does best on this measure at 80%, while France is at the bottom at 11%.The jobs concern, in other words, does not stem from general economic pessimism. The more connected Indians Ipsos surveys can be positive about the economy and still name unemployment as one of the country's most worrying problems.Ipsos switched its India consumer-confidence sample from a mixed methodology to online-only in April 2026, a break that the September report flags. Long-term comparisons therefore need caution.Do the official numbers help explain this contrasting mood?Real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, according to MoSPI estimates. Private final consumption expenditure, the broad measure of household consumption, increased 7.1%, while gross fixed capital formation rose 11.9% at constant prices. Those numbers are broadly consistent with Ipsos's strong readings for current conditions and investment sentiment.The labour market data are more mixed. The government's monthly Periodic Labour Force Survey put India's unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above at 5.0% in August on the Current Weekly Status measure, marginally lower than 5.1% in July. But the improvement came from rural India. Rural unemployment fell from 4.5% to 4.1%, while the urban rate was almost unchanged, moving from 6.7% to 6.8%. The urban Worker Population Ratio was also 47.0%, unchanged from July and below 47.5% a year earlier.These figures are not directly comparable with Ipsos's Jobs Index. PLFS measures actual labour-market status; Ipsos measures perceptions of job security and the employment environment. There is another limitation to headline unemployment numbers. NITI Aayog has also highlighted job quality, informality and underemployment as labour-market concerns, dimensions that an unemployment rate alone cannot fully capture.Taken together, the data help explain how the seemingly contradictory findings can coexist.Education is India's second-most cited concern, at 36%. That is the highest among the 30 countries, against a global country average of 13%. India's top two concerns, unemployment and education, are both closely tied to economic opportunity. The government's labour survey tracks one measure that spans both. In the latest PLFS annual report, covering 2025, 25.0% of people aged 15-29 were not in employment, education or training, or NEET . Among those aged 15-24, the share was 21.0%.The same report put the unemployment rate at 9.9% for 15-29-year-olds, 13.6% for urban youth and 6.5% for people with at least secondary education. NEET is not an unemployment measure: it also includes young people who are neither working nor studying but may not be looking for work. So for Indians, confidence in the economy, current conditions and investment is higher than in any other market. The Jobs Index is the exception, and the official data point to where some of the strain lies: among urban youth and the educated.That is the lived reality the surveys capture. The pride is collective: it is about where the country is heading. The disquiet surfaces when the conversation turns to jobs and education. With technology rapidly changing the nature of work, continuous learning and reskilling are becoming an economic necessity. But many workers and young people still lack the support, guidance and pathways needed to navigate that transition.The surveys offer a snapshot of that churn.
Article Summary: India ranks first among 30 markets on consumer confidence but 16th on jobs. Unemployment is the issue indian respondents worry about most. South africa, argentina, singapore, indonesia and chile are the only countries with a higher share of respondents citing unemployment as a worry.
